title: The Bone-Crushing Dogs That Left Only Tracks
mediaSource: Ashfall Fossil Beds Nebraska prehistoric dog tracks, Borophaginae reconstruction, fossil rhino horse camel bones tooth marks

scenes.title: Tracks from 12 million years ago
scenes.narration: At Nebraska's Ashfall Fossil Beds, researchers found tracks from a wolf-sized prehistoric predator. But this animal was no ordinary dog.
keywords: Ashfall Fossil Beds animal tracks Nebraska

scenes.title: They were called bone-crushing dogs
scenes.narration: The likely track makers belonged to Borophaginae, an extinct branch of the dog family famous for powerful jaws and teeth built to crack bones.

scenes.title: Their bite marks were there too
scenes.narration: Scientists also found tooth marks on the bones of ancient rhinos, horses, and camels that appear to match these predators' teeth.
keywords: fossil bone bite marks prehistoric predator
Nebraska Ashfall fossil rhino horse camel

scenes.title: But their skeletons are missing
scenes.narration: The strange part is that tracks and feeding evidence are present, yet no Borophaginae skeletons have been found at the site.

scenes.title: Did they arrive after the disaster?
scenes.narration: Researchers think the predators may have reached the area after volcanic ash trapped other animals, fed on the carcasses, and then escaped before dying there themselves.

scenes.title: A predator known only by its traces
scenes.narration: Twelve million years later, these predators may be telling their story through footprints and bite marks alone, revealing a lost food web without leaving a body behind.
